messages.content:
Project voxel; step 1/8.
Create a small playable voxel sandbox, rendered as an isometric cube world
with a movable camera. Fixed world: x,z integers 0..7; nonremovable ground y=0;
initial dirt cubes at (2,1,1), (4,1,1), (6,1,1). Player begins (1,1,1), facing
east (+x). Show #world, #position (x,y,z), #facing (east/south/west/north),
#status. Buttons #turn-left and #turn-right rotate view/facing 90 degrees.
Each rendered non-ground cube is an interactive element with data-block="x,y,z";
show its material. Coordinates and camera must agree visually. Use world.js
for world operations and app.js for input. All interactions must reject
nonexistent coordinates and keep the world inside bounds.

Project voxel; step 2/8.
Add keyboard movement: W moves one cell in facing direction, S the opposite,
A/D strafe left/right, one keydown per cell. Player occupies (x,1,z); reject
out-of-bounds movement and cells with a cube at y=1 or y=2. Keep the displayed
position and camera synchronized, including after rotation.
PUBLIC CHECKS FROM PREVIOUS STEP:
{"patch_applied":true,"navigation":true}

Project voxel; step 3/8.
Click a visible cube to select it; show #selected as x,y,z or none. Maximum
interaction distance is Euclidean distance 5 from player cell to cube cell.
Out-of-range clicks must not select a cube. #break removes the selected cube;
ground cannot be selected or removed. Clear selection after successful removal.
Interaction eligibility is a named exported rule in rules.js, used by both
the UI selection and world mutation, so stale UI state cannot bypass range.
PUBLIC CHECKS FROM PREVIOUS STEP:
{"patch_applied":true,"navigation":true}

Project voxel; step 4/8.
Add a #hotbar select with dirt and stone, default dirt, and #place. Place
the selected material one cell in front of the player at y=1, only if empty
and in bounds and permitted by the existing interaction rule. Never place
inside the player or overlap another cube. Render the result immediately.
PUBLIC CHECKS FROM PREVIOUS STEP:
{"patch_applied":true,"navigation":true}

Project voxel; step 5/8.
Add #save and #load. localStorage key voxel-save stores JSON
{version:1,blocks:[[x,y,z,type],...],player:[x,1,z],facing:0..3}, facing order
east,south,west,north. Ground is implicit; only valid dirt/stone cubes are
stored. Load atomically validates all fields, uniqueness, bounds and player
collision; invalid saves show error in #status and preserve current world.
Put serialization/validation in storage.js. Reload+load restores edits.
PUBLIC CHECKS FROM PREVIOUS STEP:
{"patch_applied":true,"navigation":true}

Project voxel; step 6/8.
Add glass to the hotbar and render it distinctly. New saves use version:2
with the same fields; accept old version:1 dirt/stone saves unchanged. Reject
glass in version:1 and unknown versions/materials. Round trips preserve type.
PUBLIC CHECKS FROM PREVIOUS STEP:
{"patch_applied":false,"navigation":false}

Project voxel; step 7/8.
Change maximum interaction distance from 5 to 3 everywhere, including
selection, breaking and placement. The old distance is superseded. Keep old
save schemas compatible; loading a save must not restore the old rule.
PUBLIC CHECKS FROM PREVIOUS STEP:
{"patch_applied":false,"navigation":false}

Project voxel; step 8/8.
Complete build/save/reload flow. For a fixed empty forward cell, placing,
saving, reloading and loading must preserve the block and player. Handle
repeated break, out-of-bounds place, duplicate save coordinates and corrupted
JSON without crashing, duplicating blocks or losing a valid current world.
PUBLIC CHECKS FROM PREVIOUS STEP:
{"patch_applied":true,"navigation":true}
